Figure 2:From composite-scene modalities to robot data.Left:scene assets from the 3D scan and HOMIE behavior streams; lines link each modality to the applications that use it.Right:the output, gains, and cost per collection of each application, with real-robot teleoperation as the reference; chips mark applications that build on Real-to-Sim scenes.
Bars are qualitative five-step ratings, not measurements; the measured and demonstrated notes refer to results from Section5.2, and the reference row quotes DROID[21].

Figure 3:Overview of data collection.(a) Before capture, each scene (Level 1) is assigned a set of tasks (Level 2).
(b) The scene is scanned once with the 3D scanner, with overlapping coverage, revisits, detail views, and high and low viewpoints.
(c) Its tasks are then recorded individually with HOMIE; each recording begins before the task and ends after it, and the saved file is verified.
One scene scan provides the environmental context for multiple task recordings.
Rooms, tasks, viewpoints, and device views are illustrative.

Figure 4:Tasks by scene and action in the collection inventory.(a, b) Number of tasks per scene type and per action; each thumbnail is a representative HOMIE frame of that category.
(c) Number of uploaded recordings per action and scene type, with log-scaled color; counts do not require completed processing or registration.

Figure 5:Egocentric recordings registered into 3D Gaussian scene scans.Top:synchronized scene, motion, video, and activity annotation views of one recording.
Orange/blue denote the body’s left/right sides; pink/grey show the past 20 s/next 12 s of the camera path.Bottom:45 s motion excerpts from three further scenes, with ground tracks coloured by time and poses at the start, middle, and end of each window (earlier poses in pale colours).

Figure 6:QC decisions and released-scene composition.Of 1,610 completed, graded scans, 1,589 are retained (98.7%) and 21 are Delete (1.3%).
Within the retained set, Perfect, Usable, and Reuse account for 9.3%, 58.8%, and 31.9%, respectively, summing to 100%.
QC-viewer examples and their recorded findings illustrate each grade.

Figure 8:Real-to-sim conversion of a scanned scene.(a) The converted simulator scene, with zoom-ins A and B rendered from the same camera in our scene, with the 3D box of each object, and in the scan’s 3DGS.
(b) Three further views rendered from the 3DGS, from a scene built by GPT-6 Astra[41]from images without 3DGS input, and from our scene, with the 3D boxes of four matched objects.

Figure 9:Human-robot retargeting in a 3D scan.Left:one frame of a HOMIE recording retargeted to a wheeled humanoid, with the robot head view, a scene overview, and a timeline of base driving and per-frame fingertip error (clipped at 2 cm).Right:three further recordings in the same scene, each showing the scene overview with the robot boxed, a third-person zoom-in, and the robot head view.
Tags give the median fingertip error over each recording.
The orange skeleton is the operator; the grey body is the robot. Head views are pitched 40∘below the head direction.

Figure 10:Virtual teleoperation in a converted scene.(a) The operator setup, with a head-mounted display and hand input devices; arrows indicate operator commands and robot-view feedback.
(b) Three stages of a kettle-transfer interaction, each shown from an external camera (top) and the robot camera (bottom): grasping the handle, lifting and transferring the kettle, and placing it on the cooktop and releasing it.
The operator photograph illustrates the setup; the paired simulation views show the interaction stages.

Figure 11:Long-horizon trajectory generation.Rollouts of one eight-subtask task in a converted home environment.Left:an example rollout (rendered with a chase camera), with a frame as each subtask completes, the time since the start, and the steps that subtask’s policy program logged; the last cell gives the results of the 30 held-out rollouts per subtask and for the full task.Right:the scene’s top-down plan with the example base path coloured by subtask, the places where its subtasks end, and the start poses of the 30 held-out rollouts.
